children: Eurozone government bond yields fall in early trade, moving in line with Treasury yields, even as markets continue to consider further interest-rate hikes by the European Central Bank and the Federal Reserve. "Bond markets should stabilize near-term as the data impetus looks subdued, while the focus could be on tech and geopolitical headline risk remains," Commerzbank rates strategists say in a note. A 25-basis-point rate hike by the Fed in December looks like a foregone conclusion, while the probability of similar-sized tightening by the ECB is priced at 85%, according to LSEG. On Monday, bond supply will only come from Slovakia. The 10-year Bund yield falls 1 basis point to 3.369%, according to Tradeweb. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
